messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — High GPU queue growth in us-west-gpu-pool. metric=queue_length, value=7123, threshold=500, severity=high. Auto-escalating to #incidents and paging @oncall.
Alex: I'm seeing the same on dashboards — 5m ingestion spike, throughput flat, backlog increasing. Customers hitting 429s and timeouts. Starting live triage.
Priya: Investigating autoscaler. Early signals: scale attempts are being rate-limited by provider quota and our internal scale-up cap. Logs show multiple failed scaleups and backoffs.
Priya: log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:03:12Z autoscaler INFO attempt=1 desired=24 current=8 -> scale_up_error(provider_quota_exceeded)
2026-03-15T02:03:12Z autoscaler WARN backoff=60s
2026-03-15T02:05:18Z autoscaler INFO attempt=2 desired=24 current=8 -> scale_up_error(capacity_limit_reached)
```
Maya: On-call here. Opening bridge — https://meet.redwood/incident-4960 (bridge created). Please join.
Jamal: Pinging cloud provider contacts, looks like short-term AZ quota is hit for this account in us-west-2. They're confirming and estimating 20–30m to lift.
Theo: We should immediately enable fallback routing: route non-SLA traffic to cached responses / CPU-backed cheap model to reduce GPU pressure. Can we flip routing flag?
Ingrid: I can flip a temporary feature flag to route non-critical customers to the cpu-fallback pool. Standby while I prepare list of customers marked best-effort.
Alex: Customer impact so far: 3 high-volume tenants seeing 5–10x increased tail latency, ~15% of requests returning 429s in last 10m. Incident severity should be P1.
Priya: Autoscaler config observations: min_replicas=4, max_replicas=32, but we also have a global scale-up-rate cap (max_add_per_min=6) plus provider quota. With the spike we needed ~16 extra GPUs quickly; scaler tried but hit both caps.
Priya: Quick mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily reserve preemptible nodes we have in standby 2) Increase max_add_per_min to 12 (manual toggle) 3) Push non-critical traffic to fallback CPU pool 4) Alert customers & set status page.
Maya: I'm taking incident lead. Alex you coordinate customer comms & status page. Priya/Jamal work provider escalation and node reservation. Theo/Ingrid handle routing changes. I'll coordinate bridge and runbook.
Alex: Draft status update for status.redwood.ai: "We’re experiencing degraded performance for generation endpoints in us-west due to GPU pool saturation and autoscaler throttle. Engineers are actively mitigating. Some requests may return 429 or time out. Next update in 15 minutes." Posting now.
deploy-bot: :deploy: Triggered job to increase max_add_per_min to 12 for autoscaler-config/us-west at 02:09 UTC. Job id: dj-4960-1
Priya: Provider responded — quota bump will take ~18m to approve. Meanwhile Jamal reserved 6 warm machines from our on-demand reservation (pool: standby-warm). Scheduling immediate attach to us-west-gpu-pool.
Jamal: reserve command executed: `reserve-nodes --pool standby-warm --count 6 --region us-west-2` -> attach in progress.
Ingrid: Routing toggle done: feature-flag `gpu_fallback_routing` = true. Non-SLA tags now routed to cpu-fallback pool. Monitoring traffic shift.
Theo: Observing 30% reduction in queue for generation-primary; good. Tail latency coming down slowly.
Alex: Customer comms: added note to status page and emailed top 5 paying tenants. Some replies asking for ETA — I told them 30m estimate.
Priya: Attach completed, but autoscaler still showing backoff due to provider-side allocation delays. However with the 6 reserved machines attached and routing reduction, queue dropped from 7123 -> 2100 in 8m.
Maya: Good progress. Can we temporarily increase per-customer rate limits to protect small tenants?
Theo: We can't increase limits without risking fairness. Suggest enforce stricter per-tenant caps for top-hitters — implemented as emergency throttle policy. Applying now.
Ingrid: Emergency throttle policy applied: top-10 tenants capped to 60% of previous throughput. Confirming enforcement.
Alex: Metrics: queue=1780, 95p latency down from 7.8s -> 2.9s, 429 rate down to 6%. Still above normal but improving.
Priya: Provider now shows partial quota increase; autoscaler resumed scale-up with smaller increments. Observed new nodes joining: +4 GPUs in last 4m.
Jamal: Provider confirmed full quota increase approved at 02:22 UTC. Autoscaler should reach desired capacity within ~6–8m.
Maya: That's the primary mitigation. Transitioning to recovery phase. Keep bridge open for another 15m.
Alex: I'll keep customer comms updated: posting note that mitigation in progress and estimated resolution 20m.
Priya: Root-cause quick notes for postmortem: sudden traffic spike (unknown origin) + autoscaler rate limits + provider quota constraint + lack of faster warm pool auto-attach path.
Maya: Actions to surface in postmortem: 1) Adjust autoscaler config: increase max_add_per_min default and add emergency fast-path 2) Add alert to detect provider quota exhaustion earlier (new metric) 3) Expand warm-standby pool in us-west 4) Improve routing playbook to auto-flip cpu-fallback for non-SLA 5) Add provider contact escalation runbook with fast approval steps.
Theo: I'll draft the changes for autoscaler with safety checks and a kill-switch. Priya please review before we roll.
Priya: Will review and include a test that simulates rapid queue growth to validate fast-path.
Ingrid: I'll convert the temporary routing steps into a documented runbook and add a toggle in the console.
Jamal: I'll follow-up with provider account team to secure larger permanent quotas and request a lower-latency approval path for emergency bumps.
Alex: Post-incident comms: draft status: "Mitigations applied, capacity increased, tail latency improving. We continue to monitor; customers may see intermittent errors. A full postmortem will be published within 3 business days." Posting now.
Maya: Wrapping bridge. Timeline summary:
- 02:02 UTC: ops-bot alert threshold crossed (queue ~7k)
- 02:03 UTC: autoscaler attempted scale-ups -> provider quota errors/backoff
- 02:08 UTC: bridge opened, reserve nodes requested, fallback routing enabled
- 02:12 UTC: reserved nodes attached -> partial relief
- 02:22 UTC: provider quota increased, autoscaler resumed and finished scale-up by 02:30
- 02:32 UTC: incident declared resolved (service returning to normal), bridge closed 02:40 (monitoring window)
Alex: Assigning action owners: Priya -> autoscaler fast-path & tests; Theo -> emergency throttle & autoscaler change PR; Ingrid -> routing runbook & console toggle; Jamal -> provider quotas & documentation; Maya -> postmortem writeup and timeline.
Priya: Noted. I'll start a draft RFC for autoscaler changes.
Theo: Will open a PR and tag reviewers.
Ingrid: I'll convert the notes to runbook in Confluence and link from incident ticket.
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Created incident ticket INC-4960 and linked this thread.
Alex: Thanks everyone for quick work. Marking this thread for postmortem follow-up. Closing active pager. :thumbsup:
Maya: Closing bridge now but keep monitoring for 2h. If any regression, reopen immediately. :pray:
ops-bot: Incident status changed -> RECOVERED. metrics normalized? queue_length < 300.
